home.cleanupIntro: Duplicate installs and leftovers found during the scan. Nothing here is deleted automatically: open the folder, check, then remove it yourself or through the launcher's uninstall.
grid.empty: No game matches. Press Esc to clear the search.
setup.title: Welcome to Game Hub
setup.intro: Three quick steps before Game Hub looks for your games. Nothing is scanned until you click Scan.
setup.drivesTitle: Which drives should Game Hub never read?
setup.drivesDesc: Tick removable or private drives: a USB SSD, a backup disk, a drive you share. USB drives are ticked for you, even the ones Windows calls fixed. Game Hub only looks at each drive's name and size here.
setup.launchersDesc: Found automatically through their launchers, no need to add them:
setup.foldersDesc: Folders with other games (every sub-folder counts as one game). Untick anything that isn't a game folder.
setup.scanning: Looking for your games… this can take a few minutes
setup.scanFailed: The scan didn't finish. Check logs\scan.log, then try again.
setup.noLaunchers: No launcher found yet. That's fine: add your game folders below.
setup.noFolders: No game folder found. Use Add folder, or let an AI find them.
check.excluded: On a drive Game Hub never reads
check.nested: Inside another folder in the list
check.tooBroad: Too broad: choose the folder that holds your games
ai.open: Find my game folders with an AI
ai.title: Find your game folders with an AI
ai.step1: 1. Copy this prompt and give it to the AI you use. An AI that can run commands on this PC (Claude Code, Codex, Copilot...) looks by itself; a chat AI (ChatGPT, Claude...) gives you one command to run and asks for its output.
ai.step2: 2. Paste the AI's answer here (its list of folders):
ai.nonePasted: No folder path found in the answer. Paste the AI's list of folders.
ai.privacy: Privacy: the AI provider sees your folder names, nothing else. Drives you chose never to read are named in the prompt so the AI stays away from them.
ai.p.intro: I use Game Hub, a game launcher on this Windows PC. Please find the folders on this PC where games are installed, so I can add them to Game Hub.
ai.p.never: Never open, list or search these drives, they are private: {list}.
ai.p.shape: I need folders that hold one sub-folder per game (for example X:\Games, where X:\Games\Some Game is one game). List those parent folders, not each game.
ai.p.readOnly: Only look at folder names. Don't open, run, change or delete anything.
ai.p.skip: Skip these folders, Game Hub already finds their games through the launchers:
ai.p.have: These folders are already in Game Hub:
ai.p.chat: If you can't run commands on this PC yourself, give me one PowerShell command that lists the folders two levels deep on the drives I may share, then wait for me to paste its output.
ai.p.answer: When you're done, answer with a single code block, one full folder path per line, like this:
settings.title: Settings
settings.scanDesc: {games} · last scan {date}. Run it after installing or moving a game.
settings.addGameDesc: For anything the scan missed: pick its executable and it joins the hub.
settings.coversDesc: {n} of {total} games have a cover. Missing ones are looked up on Steam, Epic and the Microsoft Store after every scan; use the pen icon for the rest.
settings.foldersDesc: Every sub-folder of these is checked for a game. Steam, Epic, EA, Ubisoft, GOG, Battle.net, Riot, Amazon, Rockstar and Xbox app games are found through their launchers wherever they are installed. Add folders for everything else.
settings.noFolders: No extra folders. Games from launchers are still found.
settings.drivesDesc: Drives marked "Never read" are never scanned, and their games, folders and executables are refused. Only fixed disks are scanned at all.
settings.noHidden: No hidden games. Use the pen icon › Hide from hub to tidy something away.
settings.minimize: Minimize Game Hub when a game starts
settings.minimizeDesc: As soon as the game's window opens, Game Hub steps aside so your mouse, keyboard and controller go straight to the game.
settings.restore: Bring Game Hub back when you quit
settings.restoreDesc: When the game has fully closed, Game Hub returns to the front.
settings.trackOutside: Count games started outside Game Hub
settings.trackOutsideDesc: Play time is always counted for games you start from Game Hub. With this on, games started from Steam, a desktop shortcut or anywhere else are counted too (a light check once a minute).
settings.controllersDesc: DualSense, DualShock 4 (also through DS4Windows) and Xbox controllers work in Game Hub: D-pad to move, Cross / A to play, Circle / B to go back, Triangle / Y for Favorites, Square / X to edit, L1 / R1 to switch tabs, Share / View to search.
settings.summon: Bring Game Hub back with the controller
settings.summonDesc: Hold View + Menu (Share + Options through DS4Windows) for 1.5 seconds, anywhere in Windows. Works with Xbox controllers and anything that appears as one.
settings.steamInputTitle: Controller not working in a Steam game?
settings.steamInputDesc: Steam decides how each game sees your controller, and Steam Input can be switched off for a single game. In Steam, open the game's controller settings (Library > right-click the game > Properties > Controller, or the controller icon while it runs) and turn Steam Input on for that game. If you use DS4Windows instead, leave Steam Input off for that game so it doesn't see two controllers.
settings.lock: Lock Game Hub to my Windows account
settings.lockDesc: This PC has other user accounts. When locked, only your account can use Game Hub; others see the page but can't launch or change anything.
settings.startupDesc: Runs the small local server in the background so the hub opens instantly.
about.title: Made by
about.bio: I build tools I want to use. Game Hub keeps every game on your PC in one place. On your machine.
about.starHint: Game Hub is free and open source. If it's useful to you, a star on GitHub helps other people find it.
about.disclaimer: Provided as is, without any warranty: you use Game Hub at your own risk. Keep your own backups of what matters, game saves first.
lang.aiNote: This translation was written by an AI and may have mistakes.
lang.enNote: The other languages were translated by an AI, and anyone can correct them.
ds4.title: DS4Windows: per-game rules
ds4.desc: Choose what DS4Windows does while each game runs. "Turn off" lets the game or Steam Input see your real PlayStation controller; DS4Windows comes back when you leave the game. Game Hub writes the rules into DS4Windows and restarts it.
ds4.notRunning: DS4Windows isn't running right now; the rules apply when it starts.
ds4.appliedN.one: DS4Windows rules saved ({n} game with a rule).
ds4.appliedN.other: DS4Windows rules saved ({n} games with a rule).
ds4.restarted: DS4Windows was restarted to load them.
ds4.notRunningNote: They apply the next time DS4Windows starts.
ds4.tip.dualsense: DS4Windows also takes over your DualSense. Most games and Steam understand a DualSense by themselves, so fewer games need a rule if DS4Windows leaves it alone: in DS4Windows, open Settings, then Device Options, and untick Enable under DualSense.
ds4.tip.hides: DS4Windows hides your controllers from games, so a game never sees one twice. Keeping it on is always safe; turn it off only for games where you want PlayStation buttons and effects.
ds4.tip.noPads: Choose how you connect your PlayStation controllers, so the suggestions fit them.
ds4.tip.steamInput: Or turn Steam Input on for this game in Steam, then DS4Windows can be off.
ds4.checkPrivacy: Check my games looks up each game on PCGamingWiki and Steam to see which controllers it understands by itself. Only game names are sent.
ds4.neverChecked: Not checked yet: the suggestions only use what Game Hub knows on this PC.
ds4.usedSuggestions.one: {n} choice changed to its suggestion. Press Apply to DS4Windows to save it.
ds4.usedSuggestions.other: {n} choices changed to their suggestions. Press Apply to DS4Windows to save them.
ds4.noSuggestions: Nothing to change: every choice already matches its suggestion.
ds4.why.native: the game reads it by itself
ds4.why.cableOnly: the game reads it only with a cable
ds4.why.xboxOnly: the game only understands Xbox controllers
ds4.why.steamInput: Steam Input is on for this game
ds4.why.steamTranslates: Steam translates it for this game
ds4.why.youDouble: You said buttons were pressed twice.
ds4.why.youFineOff: You said the controller works with DS4Windows off.
ds4.why.youFineOn: You said the controller works with DS4Windows on.
ds4.why.youNone: You said the controller didn't respond with DS4Windows off.
ds4.why.youNoneOn: You said the controller didn't respond.
ds4.why.noPads: No PlayStation controller is chosen above.
ds4.src.files: Sony's controller file in the game folder
ask.title: How did your controller work in {name}?
ask.desc: Your answer helps Game Hub choose what DS4Windows does while this game runs.
ask.offerOff: Then DS4Windows should be off while {name} runs. Turn it off for this game?
ask.offerOn: Then {name} needs DS4Windows. Keep it on for this game?
ask.thanks: Thanks. Game Hub will remember it for {name}.
ask.checkSettings: Check the controller settings inside {name}, and Steam Input if it is a Steam game.
ask.tellTitle: How does your controller work in {name}?
ask.tellOn: It works only with DS4Windows on
ask.tellDouble: Buttons press twice with DS4Windows on
backups.title: Backups
backups.desc: Game Hub saves a copy of your settings, game list, fixes, favorites, play time and custom covers once a day when something changed. Game files are not included.
backups.dataFolder: Your settings and game data are kept in {path}, apart from the program.
backups.copyToNone: Not set: backups stay in Game Hub's own backups folder
backups.none: No backups yet. The first one is made in a moment.
backups.confirmRestore: Restore the backup from {date}? Your current settings are backed up first, so you can undo this.
backups.copyToSet: Backups will also be copied to {path}
backups.copyToCleared: Backups are no longer copied elsewhere
lock.title: Game Hub is locked
lock.body: It's locked to another Windows account on this PC. If it's yours, open Game Hub from its Desktop or Start menu shortcut.
